title: PRD: Typed Stream Windows, Failure Modes, and Offline Tool Delegation Acceptance
creator: Luca Rossi
description: This ticket defines acceptance criteria for a new structured-output mode that emits typed frames in time-bounded windows, supports graceful degradation and deterministic handoff to an offline tool gateway, and exposes telemetry to diagnose partial emissions and replay. The goal is to allow product integrations to rely on eventual completion semantics while preserving low-latency stream fragments and clear failure signals.
background: Customers increasingly depend on streamed JSON-like outputs for live UIs and downstream processing. Existing contracts mix ad-hoc partial objects with opaque retries; that leads to complex client logic and unreliable tool invocations. We need a single contracted pattern: typed stream windows (TSW) + deterministic offline handoff tokens + explicit failure classes.
goals: 1) Provide a typed-frame envelope format that can be emitted incrementally with window markers. 2) Define deterministic handoff semantics for delegating to offline tool invokers when streaming cannot complete synchronously. 3) Make failure modes explicit and observable so clients can implement simple idempotent recovery.
non_goals: This ticket does not change model scoring quality, does not add new model variants, and does not implement a production offline tool executor — it only defines API contracts, server-side tokens, and acceptance tests for the platform runtime and console telemetry.
requirements: 1) Envelope: every emitted chunk must be a typed frame with keys: frame_id (uuid), type (enum: partial|checkpoint|window_end|error|tool_handoff), payload (stringified JSON), and seq (int). 2) Windowing: the runtime must announce 'window_start' and 'window_end' frames for time-bounded groups; clients must be able to reason about window boundaries without schema negotiation. 3) Checkpointing: at least one checkpoint frame must be emitted every 4KB of serialized payload or every 1s, whichever is earlier. 4) Tool handoff: when model cannot synchronously finish an operation that requires a tool, runtime must emit a tool_handoff frame containing a handoff_token (signed opaque string) and minimal explanation. 5) Idempotency: handoff_token encodes a deterministic request fingerprint; repeated handoff submissions must be safe. 6) Failure taxonomy: errors must include a failure_class (temporary|permanent|partial) and a recommended client action. 7) Observability: events for window_start/window_end/checkpoint/tool_handoff/error must be visible in Console with token-level latency and success tags. 8) Backpressure: streaming delivers at least one frame every 250ms under nominal load; if backpressure prevents emission, emit a window_end with failure_class=temporary.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Typed frames emitted - In an integration test with a 20s streaming generation, the server emits frames where every frame contains frame_id, type, payload, seq; no frame is larger than 16KB serialized.

AC-2: Window markers - For payloads that correspond to logically separable suboutputs (e.g., multi-step reply), the runtime emits window_start and window_end frames so a downstream consumer can render partial sections independently.
AC-3: Checkpoint frequency - In synthetic tests generating 20KB of payload at steady pace, at least 5 checkpoint frames are observed and spaced no more than 1s apart or 4KB in bytes.

AC-4: Deterministic handoff token - When model pauses for a long-running tool (simulated by runtime delay), a tool_handoff frame is emitted with a handoff_token. Submitting the same handoff_token twice to the offline tool gateway results in identical single application of side effects (idempotent).

AC-5: Failure classification and client guidance - Injected failures in the runtime produce frames with failure_class equal to temporary, permanent or partial and the payload includes a recommended client action string. Console shows the failure_class and recommended action in the trace.

AC-6: Backpressure escape hatch - Under configured load that simulates queue saturation, the runtime gracefully emits window_end with failure_class=temporary and a tool_handoff token when appropriate; stream does not hang indefinitely for the client.

AC-7: Observability - Every window_start/window_end/checkpoint/tool_handoff event for a trial workload is visible in Console UI with per-frame latency, frame seq, and handoff_token as masked metadata, and telemetry retention is testable in the release retention window.

AC-8: Schema compatibility - Clients using strict typed-frame parsers can ignore unknown additional top-level keys in payload without failing; a compatibility test with added experimental keys passes.

AC-9: Replay and resume - Given a recorded sequence of frames up to a checkpoint frame, a resumed stream with the same session id will allow the client to request replay from the last checkpoint using the checkpoint frame.seq reference and continue without data loss.

AC-10: End-to-end tool handoff observability - When a handoff_token is consumed by a simulated offline tool, the Console linkage shows the handoff_token lifecycle: emitted -> claimed -> completed/failed with timestamps and latency metrics.
test_cases: TC-1: Emit a 30s generated chat that contains three logical sections; assert window markers and per-window payload correctness.

TC-2: Simulate a synchronous tool timeout; confirm a tool_handoff frame with a token is emitted and that the token is accepted by a stub offline gateway which returns idempotent success on repeated claims.
TC-3: Flood the runtime to trigger backpressure and verify that the stream emits a window_end with failure_class=temporary and an explanatory message within 500ms of detection.
TC-4: Add experimental keys to payload and verify strict consumer ignores them without parse errors.
TC-5: Run observability smoke: generate streams and confirm Console traces include masked handoff_token, frame seq, and per-frame latency for at least 100 streams.
TC-6: Checkpoint replay: truncate recorded frames, request resume from last checkpoint.seq and validate continuity of seq numbers and payloads.
TC-7: Security review stub: verify handoff_token is signed with platform KMS and expires after configured TTL; token leakage mitigation tested by masking in Console UI.
TC-8: Load regression: under 95th percentile token rate, ensure average frame emission latency remains under 120ms.
dependencies: ENG-28641: runtime: envelope framing and serializer
ENG-29110: observability: per-frame traces and masking
ENG-29877: auth: signed handoff token implementation
rollout_notes: Start with a feature-flag behind 'typed_stream_windows'. Enable for 5% of hosted API traffic with synthetic telemetry. If 5% passes acceptance, increment to 25% and run load tests for 48 hours before broader rollout. Provide a migration guide for SDKs to adopt frame parsing and checkpoint resume APIs.
notes: Design todo: agree on exact signed token format with Security; runtime must provide a server-side replay endpoint to allow clients to request resume from checkpoint.seq. Consider extension to allow 'deferred_tool_priority' in handoff payload to help offline queue scheduling.
